ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: What is H in the diagram?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the right side of the image is the longitudinal section structure of a plant stem, with multiple letters using leader lines to label different tissues. The letter H is located below the figure on the right, and its leader line points to a light green, large and thin-walled cell region at the bottom inside the section, rather than the outer boundary. Reasoning: In the anatomical structure of a plant stem, the central/internal ground tissue located inside the stem and composed of relatively large thin-walled parenchyma cells is called pith. Therefore, H labels the pith.
